scholars: Ibn Kathir says 'Ad-Din' here means the Next Life and the Payback on the Last Day.
The book Al-Jalalayn says: 'Do you know who he is?' If you do not, the next ayahs tell you.
Ibn Kathir says this person is mean to the orphan. He does not give him what he has a right to. He does not feed him or treat him kindly.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says he pushes the orphan away from his own right.
Ibn Kathir says 'miskin' means a poor person who has nothing to take care of his needs. He compares this with Surah Al-Fajr, 89:17-18.
The book Al-Jalalayn says this ayah came about Al-As ibn Wa'il or Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah.
Ibn Abbas and others said this means the people who pretend. They pray when people can see them, but do not pray when alone. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says 'woe' means a very hard punishment in the Fire.

prophet: The Prophet ﷺ said three times: 'This is the prayer of the hypocrite.' He sits and watches the sun until it is almost setting. Then he stands and pecks four rakahs like a bird, and hardly remembers Allah in them. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, told by Ibn Kathir.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says 'sahun' can mean they do not pray at all, or they pray after the time is over (Masruq and Abu Ad-Duha), or they always wait until the very end of the time, or they do not pray it the right way, or they are not paying attention to its meaning.
Ata ibn Dinar said, 'Thank Allah, He said they are careless about their prayer. He did not say they are careless in their prayer.'

prophet: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever tells people about his good deed so they will hear it, Allah will make it known to people, and make him small.' (Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Amr.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says showing off means doing a good thing only so people will see it. But if someone does a good deed only for Allah and people find out, and he is happy about it, that is not showing off.
Ibn Kathir says this means they do not worship their Lord well, and they do not treat His creation well. They will not even lend things that help people and come back to them.
Ibn Mas'ud said 'Al-Ma'un' is what people give each other, like an axe, a pot, a bucket and things like that. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says it can also mean they hold back kind acts, or zakah.
